title: Acyclic primitive-grounded support graph
problem: A proof trace can be formally complete while claims and derived evidence support each other circularly.
rules: Support edges form a directed graph from primitive or derived evidence toward claims.
Any directed cycle invalidates grounded status for claims participating in that support graph.
A grounded claim must have at least one primitive-evidence ancestor in an acyclic graph.
Derived evidence may mediate support but cannot replace primitive ancestry.
invariants: A proof object must bottom out in declared primitive evidence rather than its own conclusions
boundary: Primitive ancestry is a structural condition. It does not establish that the primitive evidence is relevant, unbiased, or sufficient; those obligations remain in HF-SIM-013.
